In [[mathematics]], an '''ordered algebra''' is an [[Algebra over a field|algebra]] over the [[real number]]s <math>\mathbb{R}</math> with unit ''e'' together with an associated [[partial order|order]] such that ''e'' is positive (i.e. ''e'' &ge; 0), the product of any two positive elements is again positive, and when ''A'' is considered as a [[vector space]] over <math>\mathbb{R}</math> then it is an [[Archimedean order|Archimedean]] [[ordered vector space]].

== Properties ==

Let ''A'' be an ordered algebra with unit ''e'' and let ''C''<sup>*</sup> denote the [[cone (mathematics)|cone]] in ''A''<sup>*</sup> (the [[algebraic dual]] of ''A'') of all positive linear forms on ''A''. 
If ''f'' is a [[linear form]] on ''A'' such that ''f''(''e'') = 1 and ''f'' generates an [[extreme ray]] of ''C''<sup>*</sup> then ''f'' is a multiplicative [[homomorphism]].{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=250-257}}

== Results ==

'''Stone's Algebra Theorem''':{{sfn | Schaefer | Wolff | 1999 | pp=250-257}} Let ''A'' be an ordered algebra with unit ''e'' such that ''e'' is an [[order unit]] in ''A'', let ''A''<sup>*</sup> denote the [[algebraic dual]] of ''A'', and let ''K'' be the [[weak-* topology|<math>\sigma\left( A^{*}, A \right)</math>]]-compact set of all multiplicative positive linear forms satisfying ''f''(''e'') = 1. Then under the evaluation map, ''A'' is isomorphic to a dense subalgebra of <math>C_{\mathbb{R}}(X)</math>. If in addition every positive sequence [[order summable|of type ''l''<sup>1</sup>]] in ''A'' is [[order summable]] then ''A'' together with the [[Minkowski functional]] ''p''<sub>''e''</sub>  is isomorphic to the [[Banach algebra]] <math>C_{\mathbb{R}}(X)</math>.
